problem: Zero-shot LLM/VLM-based ObjectNav methods rely on ephemeral visual observations and metric maps and lack an explicit structural spatial memory, leading to goal confusion, redundant paths and failures in long-horizon exploration.
motivation: Topological structure is a compact, persistent form of spatial memory that captures connectivity and semantics, but its use as a dynamic memory carrier for language-driven ObjectNav is largely untapped. Letting a VLM reason over a text-serialized topological graph should enable backtracking to key nodes (e.g. a room off a hallway) when the current exploration direction is unpromising.
key_idea: Maintain an online text-based topological memory graph (nodes with position, nearby objects, room type, frontier count) alongside a semantic point cloud map, and have a VLM pick the next node and direction, which are fused with geometric affordances to select waypoints.
insight: The ablations show that the VLM and the open-vocabulary detector (GLEE) are complementary: VLM+GLEE reaches SR 0.601 versus 0.472 (VLM only) and 0.445 (GLEE only) on HM3D. Removing any node attribute hurts substantially (w/o Objects Type SR 0.503, w/o Room Type 0.510, w/o Frontiers 0.544 vs 0.601), so semantic content in the memory nodes, not just graph connectivity, drives the gain. Note the memory-vs-no-memory ablation (no topological graph at all) is not reported, only node attribute removal.
method: Semantic point cloud map: back-projects RGB-D with pose into a voxel-downsampled scene cloud and derives object (GLEE segmentation), navigable (floor-height band plus stairs, with interpolation), obstacle and frontier point clouds (Yamauchi-style frontiers on a 2D grid); built on the InstructNav codebase.

Topological memory map: nodes <id, 2D position, surrounding object classes within r_topo, room type from VLM on panorama, frontier count>; nodes are created when the agent reaches a new waypoint and merged if closer than d_merge with a collision-free straight line (merged position = centroid, earliest ID/room type kept).

VLM reasoning: GPT-4o receives target category, text serialization of the topo map, navigation history and the panoramic view, and outputs next node ID, preferred direction in the panorama, and a found flag.

Exploration-phase affordances: sum of VLM direction, selected-node frontier, global frontier, and history-avoidance affordances over navigable points, each normalized by min-max distance to the respective point set.
Target-acquisition phase: when the target is confirmed by the VLM and detector, use VLM direction plus semantic proximity affordance to the target object points.
Safety and waypoint selection: zero affordance for points near obstacles (threshold σ) and pick the argmax navigable point as the next waypoint.
Real-robot deployment: Unitree Go2 with Jetson Orin, RealSense D435i, HESAI XT-6 lidar SLAM; 9 panoramic RGB-D views on the real robot (12 in simulation).

setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D panoramas (12 views in sim) + pose
setting.action_space: waypoint selected from the navigable point cloud (affordance argmax), executed by a local controller
setting.privileged: none (uses agent pose/odometry as in standard ObjectNav)

numbers.extra: training-free; 12 panoramic views per step; built on InstructNav codebase

numbers_note: Paper does not name the split; HM3D described as 2000 episodes/20 scenes and MP3D as 2195 episodes/11 scenes, so 'val' is assumed (standard ObjectNav val). Metrics printed as fractions were converted to percent; DTG in meters.
results: TopoNav reaches SR 60.1 / SPL 34.6 / DTG 2.49 on HM3D and SR 45.5 / SPL 16.8 / DTG 4.21 on MP3D, best among training-free methods in SR/SPL/DTG on HM3D (over WMNav SR 58.1, SPL 31.2), and matches the trained SGM (60.2 SR) on HM3D while beating it on MP3D (37.7). On MP3D it edges WMNav in SR (45.5 vs 45.4) but has lower SPL than VLFM (17.5) and WMNav (17.2). A real Go2 demo shows hallway backtracking to a room node.
limitations: Real-world evaluation is only a qualitative demo with no quantitative results; the paper never ablates topological memory against no memory, and improvements over WMNav on MP3D are marginal.
Depends on costly GPT-4o calls and 12-view panoramas per step, plus GLEE detection; latency and cost are not analyzed.
Contribution claim of 'theoretical connection' is not supported by any theory; dynamic-scene/long-horizon claims are not tested with dedicated benchmarks.
